author: val
body: Viewport for pannable, zoomable canvas areas: screen/world transforms, grid snap, and zoom with nonlinear steps. Its one live consumer is apps/circuits/opening.codex, which calls 9 of the 12 names. vp-contains, vp-set-canvas and vp-snap-to-grid have no caller. Note that apps/circuits/ViewState.codex defines its own copy of 10 of these names and does NOT cite this chapter; it is dead, because circuits builds from the entry unit's cite closure rather than globbing the directory, but a bare-name grep will report it as a consumer of this chapter and it is not.

author: val
body: Negatives are snapped by magnitude and negated, NOT by the same expression as positives. Integer division truncates toward zero, so the obvious form ((val + grid/2) / grid) * grid rounds negative coordinates toward zero and lands a full grid cell wrong: measured 2026-07-28, -25 with grid 20 answered 0 where the nearest multiple is -20, and -35 answered -20 where it is -40. The fix also makes the half-way tie symmetric: 10 snaps to 20 and -10 now snaps to -20, where before it snapped to 0.

author: val
body: The old body read `shifted - shifted + (shifted / grid) * grid`. The leading `shifted - shifted` is identically zero, so it computed the right thing for positives while carrying a term that does nothing. Dead arithmetic in an expression is a fingerprint of a botched edit and is worth reading as a signal that the line was not finished, rather than as a quirk.

author: val
body: world-to-screen and screen-to-world are exact inverses at zoom 100, with or without pan, for positive and negative world coordinates. Measured 2026-07-28 against a canvas at (50,30) size 400x200: world 0 maps to the canvas centre (250,130), a pan of (7,-3) moves it to (257,127), and 137 and -137 both round-trip exactly. Above zoom 100 they are NOT exact and cannot be: the scale divides by 100 in one direction and multiplies in the other, so truncation loses sub-unit precision. That is the intended behaviour, not a defect, but it is why the round-trip rows in the test pin zoom 100.

author: val
body: Does not fit anything. It resets pan to 0 and zoom to 100, preserving only the canvas rect and grid. There is no content model in this chapter for it to measure, so it cannot fit content even in principle. The name will mislead anyone wiring a Fit button; measured 2026-07-28 and left as it is, because changing it is a decision about what the app wants rather than a defect in the arithmetic.

author: val
body: Half-open on both axes: the left and top edges are inside, the right and bottom are not. Measured on a canvas at x=50 width 400: 49 is outside, 50 inside, 449 inside, 450 outside. That is the correct convention for a pixel rect and the test pins all four boundary values, because an off-by-one here is invisible to any reading that only probes the middle.
